answer: I built a 6-spin chain (H = sum of ZZ on neighbors + sum of X, J=1, h=1, all spins up, time 1) as a 4-step Trotter circuit. I made two stretched copies by gate folding: the circuit, then (inverse, circuit) once for 3x noise and twice for 5x noise. All 3 went as one job to garnet:mock (job 01a16044-fa79-70ef-9476-d113183769a0, 100 shots, completed and validated). Mock counts are random, so I did not use them for physics. The noisy numbers came from IQMFakeGarnet (4000 shots per circuit, on a 6-qubit chain). Average magnetization: 0.128 at 1x noise, 0.085 at 3x, 0.056 at 5x. The ideal (exact evolution) is 0.204. Extrapolating back to zero noise with a quadratic Richardson fit gives 0.155. A straight line gives 0.144. The mitigated value is closer to the ideal than the raw 1x value (error 0.049 vs 0.076), which shows the principle: noise lowers the signal in a predictable way as you amplify it, so you measure at several noise levels and extend the trend back to zero noise. It recovers part of the lost signal, not all of it, because the decay is not a perfect polynomial and the shot noise grows. The ideal Trotterized circuit itself gives 0.187, so some remaining gap is Trotter error, not hardware noise.
